# 🎲 Volatility 75 Index: RSI 80/20 on a Random-Number Market

A trader shared a Deriv **Volatility 75 Index (V75)** chart: M15, RSI(14) with Ichimoku(5,2,52), and a 0.01-lot sell.

**What V75 is:** Deriv says the index is generated by a **cryptographically secure random number generator**, with a constant **75% annual volatility** and **one tick every 2 seconds**, independent of news or any real market ([Deriv blog](https://blog.deriv.com/blog/what-is-volatility-75-index-how-to-trade), [Deriv experts](https://experts.deriv.com/insights/do-brokers-manipulate-synthetic-indices)). That's a random walk by design, so **no indicator can predict its next move**.

## Test

- **Simulator:** `lab.py` rebuilds V75 from that recipe as 2-second ticks, 24/7, assembled into M15 bars. It checks out: 74.7% measured volatility and no bar-to-bar memory.
- **Rules:** the trader's rule, *sell when RSI reaches 80, buy at 20, hold until the opposite signal*, plus the 7 other variations from [`gold_rsi/`](../gold_rsi/). Each runs on **20 independent simulated years**.
- **Spread:** about 22 points (0.06% round trip). This is estimated from the trader's own screenshot: a sell from 38,912.94 showing +$0.93 while the bid was 38,797.64. Deriv's swap charges are left out, which only flatters the rules.

## Results (0.01 lot, after spread)

| Rule | Trades/yr | Win rate | Edge/trade before spread | Average year | Profitable years | Best year | Worst year |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Trader's: touch 80/20, reverse** | 69 | 14% | −0.11% | **−$56** | 35% | +$408 | −$551 |
| Touch 80/20, exit at RSI 50 | 75 | 58% | +0.05% | $0 | 50% | +$102 | −$80 |
| Confirm 80/20, exit at RSI 50 | 79 | 60% | +0.05% | −$4 | 60% | +$91 | −$114 |
| Touch 80/20, ATR stop 2 / target 2 | 81 | 51% | +0.02% | −$14 | 40% | +$60 | −$110 |

All 8 variations have an edge of about zero before costs; the small differences are noise. After the spread, every one loses on average over 20 years.

- **The same rule ranges from +$408 to −$551 a year** on the same random process. Profitable stretches are luck, not skill, and they don't predict the next stretch.
- **A high win rate isn't profit.** Exiting at RSI 50 wins about 60% of trades and still averages about $0.

## Run it

```bash
python -m v75_sim.lab           # 20 simulated years x 8 rules (~30 s)
python -m pytest tests/test_v75_sim.py
```

> ⚠️ Research project, not financial advice. On a market built from random numbers, the spread and swap make every strategy's long-run expectation negative.
